meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
You asked for this meeting, so skip the pleasantries. Was Owen heard before that mark went in, yes or no?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology, and a straight answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on who decided and whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "Thanks for coming in." gave her no answer to her opening question, so she stayed at her opening position and pressed harder.
Try next time: on your first turn, answer her question directly by admitting in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then show her a dated document from Owen's own work that she can check herself.
